title: Cohort POC Studio — Facilitator Guide & Slide Outline
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a facilitator-first guide and slide skeleton for a cohort-based POC studio: a compact, interactive multi-customer workshop we run to validate integration patterns, align on constraints, and produce prioritized next steps and a deployment proposal by the end of day. Unlike a single-customer hands-on lab, the cohort format accelerates learning through cross-team comparisons and surfaces common infrastructure blockers for Redwood Private/Dedicated deployments.

Intended outcome (by session end):
- Each participating customer leaves with a 2-page deployment proposal draft (service boundaries, latency SLO target, model selection rationale, basic cost estimate).
- SE team has 3 reusable cookbooks for common constraints (VPC peering, KV cache policies, tokenization/trim strategies).
- A prioritized backlog of follow-up PoC tasks and owners.

Duration: 4.5 hours (half-day) — recommended for up to 6 customer teams (2 reps/customer: engineering + product/ops).

Pre-work (send 7 days before):
- Short forms (15 min) for each customer: workloads, peak qps, sensitive data flag, preferred cloud/region, sample prompt set (3 examples).
- Ask customers to share any existing architecture diagrams or network constraints.
- Provide a one-pager: what to expect and what we will deliver.

Room & logistics:
- Virtual: Zoom + 1 breakout room per customer.
- Physical: large room with 6 small tables, projector, whiteboards, sticky notes.
- Tech: demo account credentials (hosted Redwood API keys with rate-limited sandbox), shared slide deck, Miro board with pre-seeded templates.

Participants and roles:
- Lead facilitator (SE): runs whole session, timekeeper, synthesis lead.
- Tech demo owner (Engineers x1): runs quick demo and answers runtime questions.
- Solutions architect (rotation): moves between tables/breakouts to unblock customers.
- Customer reps (eng + product/ops): bring workload context and decide priorities.
- Note scribe (can be customer-facing): capture decisions, owners, open questions.

Agenda (timestamps):
- 00:00–00:15  Welcome & orientation (Lead facilitator)
  - Goals, logistics, success metrics, health check.
  - Quick intro: 6 customers, 4.5 hrs, deliverables.
- 00:15–00:35  6x 2-minute lightning intros (customer reps)
  - Problem they want to solve, primary constraint (latency, cost, compliance).
- 00:35–00:55  Platform primer (Redwood highlight reel)
  - 5 min: runtime capabilities (batching, KV cache, quantization profiles)
  - 10 min: hosting options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) + when to pick each
- 00:55–01:35  Breakout #1 (Architecture mapping — 30 min)
  - Each customer maps current call flow and identifies integration points onto the provided template.
  - Deliverable: a single-page diagram + one sentence of risk.
- 01:35–01:45  Break (10 min)
- 01:45–02:25  Demo & guided tuning (40 min)
  - Live demo of Redwood tuning knobs: batching window, prefix caching, soft-fallback routing.
  - Live run: run 1 sample prompt per customer via shared sandbox and show token/cost/latency trace.
- 02:25–03:05  Breakout #2 (SLO & ops playbook — 40 min)
  - Customers define target P95 latency, cost-per-1000-tokens target, and acceptable degradation policies.
  - Create a mini runbook: alert thresholds, fallback model, owner.
- 03:05–03:35  Synthesis & cross-cutting issues (30 min)
  - Facilitator collects patterns, surfaces common infra blockers, and groups them into 3rd-party blockers vs Redwood-side fixes.
- 03:35–04:00  Proposal drafting & commitments (25 min)
  - Each customer drafts the 2-page deployment proposal template; SEs review and provide alignment comments.
- 04:00–04:15  Closeout & next steps (15 min)
  - Assign follow-ups, set PoC success criteria, schedule one-week check-in.

Slide outline (20–30 slides total suggested):
- Slide 1: Title + session goals (speak to deliverables)
- Slide 2: Agenda & logistics (include Slack channel/zoom links)
- Slide 3: Cohort map — who’s here and quick bullets about each workload
- Slide 4: Redwood at-a-glance (1-liner + diagram of runtime & control plane)
- Slide 5: When to choose Hosted / Dedicated / Private (decision matrix)
- Slide 6–8: Runtime knobs (batching, KV cache, quantization) — each slide: "What it is" / "When to use" / "Measured impact"
- Slide 9: Integration patterns (API-first, sidecar, edge request routing)
- Slide 10: Network & security checklist (VPC, peering, KMS, audit logs)
- Slide 11: Observability & SLOs (how to measure P95 token latency, cost breakdown)
- Slide 12: Demo pipeline & sandbox instructions (how to run the traces)
- Slide 13–18: Breakout templates (diagram, SLO sheet, runbook template)
- Slide 19: Common blockers & mitigations (populated during session)
- Slide 20: Proposal template (two-page outline)
- Slide 21: Follow-up cadence & owners
- Slide 22: Q&A + parking lot

Speaker notes (sample snippets):
- Lead facilitator, Slide 4: "We want you to walk away with concrete decisions — not just a list. We'll help you pick model variants and one operational pattern to validate in the next two weeks."
- Demo owner, Slide 12: "This request will show how prefix cache reduces token work — watch the green KYV cache hit rate on the trace panel and note the delta in p50/p95."

Facilitation playbook & tips:
- Timebox aggressively; use a visible timer on screen.
- Use the parking-lot for long-form issues and assign an owner immediately.
- When one customer is blocked, ask the group: "Anyone seen this before?" to encourage cross-learning.
- Encourage engineers to paste exact sample prompts into the sandbox so we can produce comparable traces.
- Emphasize data privacy: do not paste PHI into the shared sandbox; use redacted examples.

Breakout templates (what to capture):
- System diagram (1 page): external clients -> API layer -> Redwood (model + cache) -> DB / datastore.
- SLO card (one line each): target p50/p95, cost target, allowed fallback.
- Runbook stub: alert condition, runbook steps, rollback policy, owner.

Live demo checklist (Engineer):
- Confirm tenant sandbox API key + rate limit set.
- Pre-load 3 sample prompts per customer as test cases.
- Configure dashboard to show traces with token-level timing.

Success metrics (for Redwood & customers):
- Customers: complete 2-page proposal + commit to at least 1 validation task within 14 days.
- Redwood: capture 3 repeatable infra blockers and verify we can reduce time-to-solution for each by 30% within next quarter.

Follow-up artifacts (deliver within 48 hrs):
- Consolidated 1-page cohort summary (patterns + blockers).
- Individual 2-page draft proposal PDFs for each customer.
- Playbooks (network, caching, SLOs) as markdown in GH repo.

Risk register (common):
- Risk: Customer network policy blocks outbound connections to Redwood sandbox.
  - Mitigation: Provide an on-demand private demo VPC or local mock with recorded traces.
- Risk: Customers bring production-sensitive prompts.
  - Mitigation: Enforce redaction policy; offer to run sensitive tests in Private deploy evaluation.

Materials to send post-session:
- Deck PDF with filled canvases.
- Links to sandbox traces and dashboards.
- JIRA tickets for follow-ups with owners and due dates.

Appendix: 2-page proposal template (quick sketch)
- Page 1: Customer context & success criteria (two bullets), integration diagram, traffic profile (qps, avg tokens)
- Page 2: Proposed infra (hosted/dedicated/private + region), chosen model(s) + rationale, SLOs & rollback strategy, estimated cost band (range), 4-week validation plan with owners.

Quick facilitator scripts (copy/paste):
- Kickoff: "Thanks everyone — we'll run fast and leave you with a ready-to-review proposal. If you want deep dives after this session, we'll book office hours next week."
- During synthesis: "Room to be candid — tell us what will keep this from shipping. We'll group similar issues and commit actions against them now."

That's the working facilitator guide. Add notes from run to this doc and we will version as _v1, _v2 after each cohort.
